story.iWant: four defender policies compared under the same attacks at calibrated scale
story.soThat: the note can say which defense survives, at what cost, and how fast
story.tasks: - Config and defender (AC: 1) - Policy scenarios and sweep (AC: 2, 3) - Chart (AC: 4) - Results, ADR, figures, close out (AC: 5–8)

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: See story file ACs 1–8. The five-sub-sweep design is the default; a `base` axis is an allowed alternative if proposed in the ADR and existing specs expand identically. Build one, not both.

existing.reason: Add buy, max_spread_bps with defaults that keep hashes.

story-context.constraints: - No kernel/ or protocol/ changes; PHASE_ORDER_VERSION stays 1; every existing scenario hash unchanged. - Policy files differ from calibrated-baseline only in the defender block (diff them in the Debug Log). - Charts read parquet + manifest only; no hand-tuned axes. - 1992 not re-run (3.3). - Python 3.12-compatible.

interfaces.interface: runs five sweeps; writes policies.parquet + manifest

tests.standards: pytest; defender buy=False never emits defend_buy (manual phases per 1.7); hash test; synthetic policies.parquet for the chart; policy files load and differ only in the defender block (test diffs the dumped configs).
